items.title: The ideal of the Bockstein operators is finitely generated and its quotient makes the shifted complex have locally free cohomology
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement collects five facts about the ideal J of the Bockstein operators attached to a bounded complex of finite free modules over a nonzerodivisor, among them its finite generation, the finite presentation of the quotient C, the vanishing of J along a locus described in two equivalent ways, and the local freeness of the cohomology of the shifted complex after tensoring with C (statement lines 28197-28228). The proof identifies the two descriptions of the locus, then proves the finiteness from boundedness of the complex, then obtains the vanishing of J on the locus by localizing and using that the shifted terms are finite locally free, so that the localized reduction splits in a way compatible with the map (1, d^i) and the universal property of J_i applies (proof lines 28230-28259). The final part is proved by exhibiting two diagrams whose horizontal arrows are compatible with direct sum decompositions, which identifies the differential as an injection of a summand and makes the cohomology a quotient of finite projective modules (proof lines 28264-28305). The counted span refers three times to earlier lemmas of the same section, all carried as navigation stubs.

primary.label: author lemma environment with its own label lemma-eta-vanishing-beta-plus (canonical tag 0F81), with the two descriptions of the locus E and the five numbered assertions (source lines 28197-28228)

proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: the identification of the two descriptions of E and part (4) from the vanishing beta lemma, the finiteness of J from boundedness, the proof of (3) through the local splitting compatible with the map (1, d^i), and the proof of (5) through the two Xy-pic diagrams and the direct sum decomposition (source lines 28230-28306)
